sentences.text:
The State Represented By The Special ... vs T.Bale Setti on 4
October, 2024
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.287 of 2016
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer and Sri Gokula Rama Rao, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer aggrieved by the order and decree dated 19.12.2015 passed in LAOP.No.945 of 2010 on the file of the II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court').

entities.text: II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. In nut-shell, the facts of the case are that on a requisition made by the Executive Engineer, SRSP Stage-II Thorrur, lands to an extent of 988 square yards in Sy.No.93 of Laxmiguda Village,
Rajendranagar Mandal, belonging to the respondents/ claimants were acquired for development of P7 road from Mailardevally to Srisailam Highway via Jalpally; that Draft Notification under 2 AKS,
J & LNA, J Section 4(1) of the Act was published in A.P. Gazette on 21.04.2007; that Draft Declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published in A.P. Gazette on 15.10.2007 and that after following the procedure prescribed under the Act and after conducting enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer passed Award, vide Proc.No.C/15/2007, dated 11.01.2008, fixing the market value of the acquired lands @ Rs.825/- per square yard.
4. Not being satisfied with the Award, the respondents/ claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was referred to the competent civil Court and numbered as L.A.O.P.No.945 of 2010 on the file of the Reference Court.
5.
Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, P.W.1 was examined and Exs.A-1 to A-5 were marked.
On behalf of the appellant-Referring Officer, R.W-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award was marked.

6. On due appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Reference Court enhanced the market value of the acquired to Rs.1,200/- per square yard, apart from 3 AKS, J The State Represented By The Special ... vs T.Bale Setti on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2896625/
1 & LNA, J
granting other statutory benefits under the Act to the respondents/claimants.
Aggrieved thereby, the present appeal is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

7. Learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer contended that the Reference Court erred in awarding compensation on yardage basis when vast extent of Acs.1.02 guntas was acquired, which includes the subject land belonging to the respondents/claimants; that the Reference Court has erred in placing reliance on the orders passed in LAOP.No.515 of 2008 and thereby, enhancing the compensation based on the said orders; that the Reference Court has not properly appreciated the documentary evidence adduced before it; and that therefore, the impugned order is irregular and contrary to law and accordingly, the same is liable to be set aside.

8. Learned counsel for the respondents-claimants contended that the Reference Court has appreciated the evidence adduced by the respondents/claimants in support of their claim for enhancement of compensation in a correct perspective and on finding that the respondents/claimants were able to establish their 4 AKS, J & LNA, J claim by adducing cogent evidence to that effect, rightly enhanced the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer and passed the impugned order fixing market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis.

Therefore,
the impugned order passed by the Reference Court is based on proper appreciation of facts of the case and the evidence adduced before it and as such, the same needs no interference by this Court.
9. The respondents/claimants to substantiate their claim for enhancement of market value of the acquired lands have adduced evidence by way of examining PW-1 and got marked Exs.A-1 to A-5.

10. Ex.A-3 is sale deed, dated 07.06.2007, i.e., it was executed two months after issuance of 4(1)
notification.

Ex.A-4 and A-5 are sale deeds, dated 14.05.2008 and 21.07.2008, respectively, i.e., they were executed post-notification and hence, they do not fall under the zone of consideration for determination of fair and reasonable market value of the acquired land and the same are accordingly discarded.
5 AKS, J & LNA, J 11.
The respondents/claimants mainly relied on Exs.A-1 and A-2-decree and order passed by the Reference Court in LAOP.No.515 of 2008.
The subject lands covered in the said O.P. which are situated in Sy.No.96 of Laxmiguda Village were also acquired by the Government for development of P7 road from Mailardevpally to Srisailam Road.
12. Thus, the location and the purpose of acquisition of the subject acquired lands and the lands covered in O.P.No.515 of 2008 are same/identical.
13. Therefore, the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. v. State of Jammu and Kashmir 1 is squarely applicable to the present case.

entities.text: Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. v. State of Jammu and Kashmir 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said judgment, it is held as under:-
The State Represented By The Special ... vs T.Bale Setti on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2896625/
2 "When the lands are more or less situated nearby and when the acquired lands are identical and similar and the acquisition is for the same purpose, it would not be proper to discriminate between the landowners unless there are strong reasons."
14.

entities.text: State Represented By The Special ... vs T.Bale Setti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the above judgment, since the subject acquired lands are situated nearby to the lands covered under (2017) 4 SCC 717 6 AKS, J & LNA, J Exs.A-1 and A-2 and the purpose of acquisition in both the cases is same and further, since both the lands fall in the same alignment and also, in order to maintain parity, this Court feels that it would not be proper to discriminate in fixation of market value of acquired lands.

15. Even in the sale statistics collected and referred to by the Land Acquisition Officer in the Ex.B-1-Award, there is mention of sale transactions relating to land in Sy.No.114, where the sale consideration therein works out to Rs.1,200/- per square yard.

However, the Land Acquisition Officer, without assigning any proper reasons, discarded the same and did not consider the same as comparable sale for fixation of fair market value of the acquired land.

16. As regards the contention of the learned Government Pleader for Appeals regarding fixation of market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis instead of yardage basis, as observed by the Reference Court, it is discernable from record that in the instant case, an extent of 988 square yards of lands were acquired, which itself shows that the said land was being used for other than 7 AKS, J & LNA, J agricultural purposes, therefore, the respondents/claimants are entitled to compensation for the acquired lands on yardage basis.

17. In the light of the above discussion, this Court holds that the impugned order passed by the Reference Court is based on evidence placed on record and the Reference Court has not committed any illegality or irregularity in enhancing the market value of the acquired lands to Rs.1,200/- per square yard.
18.
Therefore, this Appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.
No costs.
19. As a sequel, interim order dated 24.04.2017 passed in LAASMP.No.991 of 2016 stands vacated.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
